Why this National union page differs
Provenance precedes performance because cross-centre deduplication defines the national denominator. The field view uses SJR areas/categories for every record; WoS/JCR categories remain on WoS-only pages so two taxonomies are never mixed. Researcher evidence is shown in parallel source-defined panels; counts are not added until ORCID/Scopus Author ID/WoS RID reconciliation is complete.
Two centres, one national count. TRUBA (TÜBİTAK ULAKBİM) and UHeM (İstanbul Technical University) are, as far as this project is aware, the two HPC centres serving Turkish research at national scale -- this page is the union of their acknowledgment corpora, each itself already a Scopus+WoS union (see the per-centre combined pages). If a third national or regional centre exists, it is not tracked here, and this total should be read as "the two centres we track", not "all of Turkish HPC".

288 papers acknowledge both centres and are counted once here, not twice -- simply adding TRUBA's 2,768 and UHeM's 843 would overstate the national total by exactly that many. Quartiles are SCImago SJR throughout (not the WoS/JCR table used on the WoS-only pages), matching every other combined page on this site. Open access is on OpenAIRE's definition here — gold, hybrid, bronze, green or diamond, looked up by DOI over every article in this corpus — because this page carries that colour and OpenAIRE sees repository copies that Scopus's and WoS's publisher-side flags do not. The per-database dashboards keep those native flags and therefore report a lower share; the breakdown below shows the whole distribution. Click any tile, bar, or chart segment below for a quick paper list, or use the full national paper table below.

The gaps are not confined to marginal work. Of the ten most-cited articles here, 5 were found only by Web of Science and 3 only by Scopus — each invisible to a study using the other database alone. The single most-cited article in this corpus — Two- and One-Dimensional Honeycomb Structures of Silicon and Germanium (2009, 3,060 citations) — was found only by Web of Science, so a Scopus-only study would not report it at all.

Open-access colour (OpenAIRE, enriched over the whole union)

gold/hybrid/bronze/green/diamond from the OpenAIRE Graph, looked up by DOI across every article in this combined corpus (Scopus and WoS-only alike) — 3,275 of 3,323 matched.
The headline "Open access (OpenAIRE)" tile above is this breakdown: everything except Closed. 48 articles have no DOI match in OpenAIRE and fall back to the Scopus/WoS native flag, the only signal left for them.

Why the per-database pages report a much lower share. Scopus's openaccess flag and WoS's journal_oas_gold are publisher-side: they see the version of record, not a repository deposit. On this corpus they call 845 articles open where OpenAIRE calls 2,085 open, and green — 1,039 papers here — is most of that difference. Neither number is wrong; they answer different questions, so this page states which one it is using.

Identity rule. A source identity is not presented as the same person in the other database without an exact persistent identifier or reviewed crosswalk. This can split one person across panels, but avoids the more serious error of merging homonyms.

Browse all 3,323 articles

Searches titles, journals, years and DOIs across the entire deduplicated corpus. Centre filters include papers credited to both centres where appropriate; database provenance reports which index found the record.
Click a column heading to sort.
Method. Union of TRUBA's and UHeM's Scopus+WoS acknowledgment corpora (journal articles only), merged on DOI (or a normalised title for the handful without one). A paper acknowledging both centres is counted once. Citations are the higher of the two databases' counts, never the sum. Quartiles, broad areas and detailed fields are SCImago SJR throughout. OA colour is OpenAIRE's, by DOI, over the whole corpus. Institution, country and field rankings use whole counting, so a multi-institution, multi-country or multi-category paper can contribute once to each applicable group.

Important interpretation. Large source-level citation differences do not by themselves show a citation-counting error: Scopus and WoS retrieve different acknowledgment-defined paper sets, and a small number of highly cited source-exclusive papers can dominate a year. The repository findings log records worked DOI-level checks, including the tested absence of WLCG collaboration papers from the direct TRUBA acknowledgment corpus. WLCG is excluded from this national total because its attribution method is collaboration membership rather than centre acknowledgment.
